items.title: Charles L. Dufour Interview, 1958-05-14
items.q: pull your hair out over the screeches of Mr. Presley in that raucous school of so-called entertainment

ctx.x: So jazz has actually meant absolutely nothing in my life in my musical experience. It's meant nothing to me. On the other hand, it has never I have never felt that it offended me. See what I mean? That way you can pull your hair out over the screeches of Mr. Presley in that raucous school of so-called entertainment. Heck, I liked it. We used to go at the ballpark, for example, the old days, the baseball park. I remember going back in the 1926, 27, and every Sunday at the Double Heaven, they'd have a band in the…

used to be a regular feature on some of those when you had eight and ten. That's when baseball was eight and ten, twelve thousand people on a Sunday. When was that during the 20s? You're in the great days of the 20s, yeah. I'd say
